name: SigmaCLI
observations: npm package name: sigma-cli
Current version: 0.9.0
Binary: sigma — pattern: sigma {domain} {action} [options]
TypeScript source compiled to dist/; entry point: bin/sigma.js
Node.js requirement: >=18.0.0
Install globally: npm install -g sigma-cli (or npm link from local source if not published)
Version is defined in src/config.ts SIGMA_VERSION and package.json version — both must stay in sync
Source repo: sigma-ecosystem (TypeScript/Node.js npm package implementing the Sigma governance protocol)
Source: package.json, src/config.ts

name: SigmaSkillFiles
observations: Governance role skill files: arc, fmn, dev, aud (4 governance roles + report utility)
Platform claude_code: ~/.claude/commands/ with .md extension — invoked as /arc /fmn /dev /aud /report
Platform codex: ~/.codex/skills/ with no extension — invoked as #arc #fmn etc.
Platform reasonix: ~/.reasonix/skills/ with .md extension
Platform antigravity: ~/.gemini/agents/ with .md extension
Source files: setup/targets/{platform}/ in sigma-ecosystem repo
ROLE_FILES map in src/commands/setup.ts defines platform→role→filename mapping
/report is universal read-only Director briefing; NOT a governance role; does not switch roles; chat-only output
sigma setup install deploys role skill files per detected platform interactively; --yes flag is non-interactive
Skill files enforce role isolation: valid governance roles are ARC, FMN, DEV, AUD only
Role activation must preserve role immutability within a session; switching between governance roles requires a new session

name: SigmaSetup
observations: Global dir: ~/.sigma/ — contains templates/, rules/, governance/, bridge/, projects.json, sigma.config.json, memory_sigma.jsonl
sigma setup install: creates ~/.sigma/ structure; copies templates/rules/constitution/protocol; deploys role skill files per platform; deploys hook guard (Claude Code only)
sigma setup update: refreshes ~/.sigma/ templates/rules/governance only — does NOT redeploy skill files to AI tool directories
sigma setup memory: creates .mcp.json in project dir; creates ~/.sigma/memory_sigma.jsonl if absent; seeds it from bundle if empty; prints MCP config snippet
sigma setup memory --vscode: also writes .vscode/mcp.json for VS Code extension
sigma setup memory --reseed: overwrites memory_sigma.jsonl with fresh seed from package bundle regardless of existing content
Memory seed bundled at setup/sigma-memory-seed.jsonl inside the npm package
Hook guard: setup/targets/hooks/protect-sigma.js — blocks direct edits to Sigma/progress.json via PreToolUse hook in ~/.claude/settings.json
sigma project start --id ID --name Name: creates Sigma/ folder, progress.json, bridge files at project root; registers in ~/.sigma/projects.json
Project ID rules: uppercase letters, digits, hyphens only; max 12 characters
sigma project sync --confirm: updates governance files inside an existing project from current package

name: SigmaLifecycle
observations: Four phases: START → DESIGN → BUILD → CLOSE
DESIGN phase: ARC drafts DIR-INTENT; complete when DIR-INTENT LOCKED
BUILD phase: FMN drafts FMN-PLAN (locked before DEV begins); DEV drafts DEV-EXEC; iterative
CLOSE phase: Director authors DIR-CLOSE with explicit PLAN and EXEC version references
Gate 1: DIR-INTENT LOCKED required before sigma roadmap new
Gate 1.5: ACTIVE ROADMAP required before sigma plan new (non-pending); pending plans bypass Gate 1.5 and can be staged any time after Gate 1
Gate 2: FMN-PLAN LOCKED required before sigma exec new
Gate 3: full INTENT→PLAN→EXEC LOCKED chain required before sigma close new
Artifact versioning — Tier 1 (DIR-INTENT, DIR-CLOSE): v1.0/v1.1/v2.0, single-active, auto-supersede on new lock
Artifact versioning — ROADMAP: DRAFT → ACTIVE via sigma roadmap activate; prior ACTIVE demoted to INACTIVE; does NOT use v1.0/v1.1 lock semantics
Only one ROADMAP version may be ACTIVE at a time
Artifact versioning — Tier 2 (FMN-PLAN, DEV-EXEC): v0.1/v0.2/v0.3, multi-active, manual supersede only
STALE_INTENT: FMN-PLAN or DEV-EXEC referencing a superseded DIR-INTENT; sigma close new requires --ack-stale-intent flag
Roles: ARC (DESIGN), FMN (BUILD), DEV (BUILD), AUD (advisory, all phases)
Role immutability: cannot switch between ARC/FMN/DEV/AUD within a session; new session required
Director is sole lock authority — no AI role may lock any artifact without explicit Director authorization

LOCKED finalizes governance state for gate purposes — minor typo/format corrections may be made with Director awareness; substantive scope or evidence changes require a new version, supersession, or explicit Director-approved correction path
Only progress.json is off-limits to direct edits; artifact markdown files may be corrected in place only for minor changes with Director awareness
AI roles must NOT create a new artifact version just to make minor corrections to a LOCKED document; new version is for substantive governance-scope changes
sigma plan new resolves the LOCKED intent version (not active_version which may be a newer DRAFT) — searches intent.versions.find(v => v.state === LOCKED)
sigma exec new resolves the newest LOCKED plan version (not active_version) — searches plan.versions.filter(v => v.state === LOCKED).at(-1)

ROADMAP reconciliation: every official FMN-PLAN version must have exactly one matching ROADMAP H2 Stage section; sigma roadmap reconcile --check detects progress.json ↔ ROADMAP document mismatch; --fix appends missing stage stubs
Write-order invariant: artifact files must be written before progress.json in any command; if artifact write fails, progress.json must not be mutated
Roadmap activation atomicity: sigma roadmap activate demotes prior ACTIVE to INACTIVE and promotes target DRAFT to ACTIVE in a single progress.json write; post-condition is exactly one ACTIVE ROADMAP
Source: SIGMA_PROTOCOL.md Sections 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 11; Phase 2 corrections merged

name: SigmaMemoryArchitecture
observations: sigma-memory MCP stores reusable Sigma ecosystem constants only — not project decisions, not session notes, not derived protocol copies
~/.sigma/memory_sigma.jsonl is the global memory file; written by agents via MCP tools under Director awareness; no lock event or CLI command auto-writes to it
memory_sigma.jsonl is advisory only — never authoritative over SIGMA_CONSTITUTION, SIGMA_PROTOCOL, role rules, progress.json, CLI output, or locked artifacts
If memory conflicts with current protocol, CLI output, or runtime state: memory is stale; correct the memory and act on current state instead

Operational orientation order: (1) sigma session bootstrap; (2) SIGMA_PROTOCOL.md for doctrine; (3) role rule file for active role; (4) progress.json via CLI output; (5) ROADMAP/FMN-PLAN/DEV-EXEC artifacts; (6) memory_sigma.jsonl only for reusable ecosystem constants
MCP server for global memory: sigma-memory (@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory); for planning: sequential-thinking (@modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking)
Both MCP servers configured via .mcp.json in project root (created by sigma setup memory)

name: SigmaCLICommands
observations: Domains: project, session, intent, plan, exec, close, roadmap, git, setup, gitignore, config, sync, send, inbox, override
sigma session bootstrap [--role ARC|AUD|FMN|DEV]: outputs lifecycle phase, artifact states, gate status, next valid ops
sigma intent: new | review | lock | status | list
sigma plan: new [--pending] | promote | activate --v <ver> | audit | lock | supersede --v <ver> --reason <str> | queue | status | list
sigma plan activate --v <ver>: set an existing DRAFT plan version as active for display/status; lock order remains FIFO regardless
sigma exec: new | audit | lock | supersede --v <ver> --reason <str> | status | list
sigma close: new [--ack-stale-intent] | audit | lock | status
sigma roadmap: new | activate --v <ver> | render | reconcile [--check|--fix] | list
sigma config: show | set language <lang>
sigma sync: progress | roadmap
sigma send: --from <role> --to <role> --type <type> --subject <str> --message <str> [--reply-to <id>] [--attach <file>]
sigma inbox: --role <role> [--all] | read <id> | archive <id> | check
sigma git evidence: read-only; outputs branch, latest commit, changed files, diff stat
sigma override --reason <str> --director-confirm: bypass current lifecycle gate under Director authority; records audit entry in Sigma/memory/overrides.jsonl

Command authority classes: Read-only (any role) | Draft/Operational (within role boundary) | Approval (explicit Director authorization required) | Risk/Supersession (explicit Director authorization required)
Lock commands always require explicit Director authorization: approved / lock it / go ahead / run it / confirmed
Ambiguous signals not sufficient for lock: okay / noted / makes sense / looks good
Source: SIGMA_PROTOCOL.md Section 23, Section 16A; src/commands/*.ts (Phase 2)

name: SigmaProjectStructure
observations: Sigma/ governance folder at project root — separate from all source code

Sigma/ subfolders: design/ (DIR-INTENT), build/ (FMN-PLAN, DEV-EXEC, ROADMAP), close/ (DIR-CLOSE), rules/ (role rules), logs/ (progress backups, migration logs), memory/ (overrides.jsonl only); messages/ (role inboxes: messages/{toRole}/, index at messages/index.json, attachments at messages/attachments/)
Sigma/progress.json: CLI-managed runtime state — agents MUST NOT edit directly; use sigma commands
Sigma/memory/overrides.jsonl: CLI-written audit log for sigma override commands; agents read but do not write
Sigma/rules/ files: ARC-RULE.md, AUD-RULE.md, FMN-RULE.md, DEV-RULE.md — read-only during execution
Sigma/templates/: artifact templates for DIR-INTENT, FMN-PLAN, DEV-EXEC, DIR-CLOSE, ROADMAP, MSG
Bridge files at project root: CLAUDE.md (Tier 1 Full), GEMINI.md (Tier 1 Full), AGENTS.md (Tier 1 Full), DEEPSEEK.md (Tier 2 Lightweight), REASONIX.md (Tier 3 Shell Whitelist)
Source code, tests, scripts, and deliverables live OUTSIDE Sigma/ — Sigma governs, does not own work product
sigma-ecosystem is the project where Sigma governs itself: governance terminology may appear in product code by exception
Source: SIGMA_PROTOCOL.md Section 12

name: SigmaMailboxBehavior
observations: Valid messaging roles: ARC, FMN, DEV, AUD — DIRECTOR is not a valid sender or recipient in Sigma role messaging
A role may not send a message to itself (no self-send)
sigma send unread gate checks the SENDER (fromRole), not the recipient — a role cannot send while ignoring its own inbox
If FMN has unread messages, FMN is blocked from sending to anyone until FMN reads them
A sender with no unread can send to any recipient regardless of that recipient inbox state
Sender can send multiple messages to the same recipient — no restriction on recipient inbox depth
Policy error format: SEND BLOCKED — {fromRole} has N unread message(s) in their own inbox
Recovery hint in error: sigma inbox --role {fromRole} to list unread; sigma inbox read <id> to mark read
sigma inbox --role <role>: lists unread for that role; sigma inbox read <id>: marks message READ; sigma inbox archive <id>: marks ARCHIVED
Message status lifecycle: UNREAD → READ → ARCHIVED; ARCHIVED hides from default inbox but is not deleted

Role-to-role messages can request handoff, review, clarification, revision, or advisory response — they never constitute Director approval, artifact lock authorization, risk acceptance, supersession, or closure authorization
Messages are stored in Sigma/messages/{toRole}/ as markdown files; index at Sigma/messages/index.json
Source: src/commands/send.ts (getUnreadForRole checks fromRole), src/commands/inbox.ts
